title: An MLIR pipeline for offloading Fortran to FPGAs via OpenMP
problem: HPC applications written in Fortran lack efficient pathways for offloading compute kernels to FPGAs for acceleration, requiring custom compilers and limiting portability.
motivation: With Moore's Law slowing, heterogeneous computing platforms (FPGAs) become essential for HPC workloads. Existing OpenMP FPGA efforts rely on custom compilers, hindering adoption and maintainability. MLIR offers composability and portability benefits.
method: This compiler pipeline is built on MLIR (a flexible compiler framework that can work with multiple 'dialects' or specialized instruction sets). It takes Fortran code parsed by the Flang frontend and transforms it using MLIR at multiple levels, combining the OpenMP dialect (for multi-core parallel computing) with the HLS dialect (High-Level Synthesis—tools that turn code into hardware descriptions). The HLS backend then generates the actual hardware logic for FPGAs (field-programmable gate arrays, chips that can be reconfigured to perform different computational tasks). Programmers mark which code sections run on the FPGA using OpenMP target directives (standard annotations for parallel computing), and can manually optimize individual kernels for performance.
key_novelty: This is the first compiler to selectively offload Fortran code to FPGAs using standard OpenMP target directives, by combining hardware-synthesis and parallel-computing tools within MLIR (a compiler platform built to work with multiple target hardware platforms).
contributions: First OpenMP FPGA offloading implementation integrated with MLIR
MLIR OpenMP + HLS dialect composition for portable FPGA compilation
Support for Fortran via Flang frontend
Extensible framework for directive-based FPGA acceleration
Manual kernel optimization via standard OpenMP directives
limitations: No performance evaluation or benchmarking results presented. Scalability to complex kernels unclear. Code availability only through GitHub (xdslproject/ftn), not formally evaluated.
